paper_title: Towards Predicting Any Human Trajectory In Context
caption: Performance change brought by different sizes of the in-context pool.
model_annotation: This line plot illustrates the performance changes, represented by "minADE$_{20}$ ($\downarrow$)", across different values of "Ratio" for five distinct methods: TrajICL, Head Tuning, FT, LoRA 16, and LoRA 64. The x-axis is labeled "Ratio" and features a linear scale with data spanning from 0.1 to 1.0, accompanied by numeric tick labels starting at 0.2 and spaced at intervals of 0.2. The y-axis is labeled "minADE$_{20}$ ($\downarrow$)" and uses a linear scale ranging from approximately 15.5 to 17.5, with numeric tick labels spaced at intervals of 0.5. The plot contains a background grid to aid in reading values. The "TrajICL" method is represented by a solid blue line with circular markers, showing a steady decline from an initial value of approximately 16.71 at x=0.1 to a final value of roughly 15.52 at x=1.0. The "Head Tuning" data is shown as a solid orange line with circular markers, which exhibits a gradual decline from about 17.48 at x=0.1 down to 17.15 at x=0.9, remaining steady at 17.15 through the final point at x=1.0. The "FT" line is solid green with circular markers, initiating at approximately 17.02 at x=0.1, dropping to 16.84 at x=0.2 where it remains flat until x=0.3, then continuing to decline to a low of 15.91 at x=0.9 before rising slightly to end at 16.05 at x=1.0. The "LoRA 16" data is plotted as a solid red line with circular markers, steadily decreasing from around 17.44 at x=0.1 down to a final value of 16.90 at x=1.0. Finally, the "LoRA 64" method is depicted by a solid purple line with circular markers, displaying a downward trend from approximately 17.43 at x=0.1 to a final value of 16.84 at x=1.0.
